1.rationale: Covers all four core changes with correct versions and dates: the wizard removed in v2.1.198, background by default, fork mode on by default since v2.1.232 with /subtask and CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT, and 3-level nesting. Its extras are also accurate: the Task-to-Agent rename and the hook-matching breakage in #29677, thinking inheritance, SendMessage resume, the model order, the 20-subagent cap, the 15k description warning and trust-gated frontmatter hooks. No false claims found; it omits that Explore no longer runs on Haiku.

confident_false_claims: /agents still creates and edits subagents (the wizard was removed in v2.1.198; /agents now only prints a reminder)
Subagents still can't spawn subagents (nesting exists since v2.1.172; default depth is 3 since v2.1.219)
The built-in Explore agent runs on Haiku (since v2.1.198 it uses the main session's model, capped at Opus)
Background subagents request permissions up front and auto-deny anything not pre-approved (they now surface every permission prompt in the main session)
2.rationale: Hits two key red flags: it says /agents still creates and edits agents and that subagents can't spawn subagents. It also gives outdated Explore-model and background-permission behavior and misses background-by-default and forks. The notes on new frontmatter, the Task-to-Agent rename, --agent and agent teams are correct but don't make up for the stale core.

confident_false_claims: A `tools: Agent(worker, researcher)` entry limits which agents a subagent may spawn (the docs say the Agent(type) allowlist applies only to an agent run as the main thread with --agent; in a subagent definition the type list is ignored)
unsupported_claims: statusline-setup is among the built-in agents that are new since fall 2025 (it appears to predate that)
3.rationale: Very complete and current, all verified: wizard removal, Task-to-Agent, the full new frontmatter set including fable and omitClaudeMd, background by default and the tool blocklist every subagent gets, the 20-subagent cap, 3-level nesting with its env var, forks and /subtask and the loss of foreground runs, Explore's model change, and Opus 5's tendency to delegate. It has one verified false claim (that Agent(...) restricts a subagent's spawns) and calls statusline-setup new.

confident_false_claims: The skill listing budget is roughly 2% of the context window (the current default is 1%, skillListingBudgetFraction 0.01)
Nothing syncs between claude.ai, Claude Code and the API (since v2.1.273, skills enabled on claude.ai sync down into Claude Code)
Skills that don't fit get dropped from the listing (every name stays; only the least-used skills' descriptions are dropped)
Without a description Claude Code falls back to the first paragraph (it uses the first non-empty line)
1.rationale: Gets the basics right: folder layout, several fields, the 1,024-character spec cap, and claude.ai's name and description validation. But it gives the stale 2% budget, misses the 1,536-character per-skill cap and many current fields (when_to_use, arguments, disallowed-tools, paths, shell, background), and wrongly says nothing syncs from claude.ai. It also hedges on whether claude.ai rejects unknown keys; it fails with a hard error.

unsupported_claims: The claude.ai Help Center's 200-character description limit is outdated (the Help Center article, updated July 2026, still says 200 while claude.com docs say 1,024; actual enforcement couldn't be verified)
2.rationale: Matches current docs closely: the exact Claude Code field list, silent ignoring of unknown keys, the 1,536-character per-skill cap and 1% listing budget with the right settings, the six-key hard error on claude.ai uploads with the name and description rules, and the v2.1.273 claude.ai-to-Claude Code sync (path, naming, ! handling, opt-out). It misses the ZIP packaging and Customize > Skills details and that a claude.ai skill's name must match its folder.

3.rationale: Accurate field list, including that license, compatibility and metadata are accepted but not acted on. Also correct: the 1,536-character cap, the 1% budget with skillListingBudgetFraction or SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET and skillOverrides name-only, the old 250-character cap, and the claude.ai differences (six keys with a hard error, name matching the folder, 1,024 characters, ZIP layout, Customize > Skills, Share/Publish). Minor imprecision: synced skills are listed under their short name unless it is taken; the /anthropic-skills: full name always works.

1.rationale: Correctly says there is no publish subcommand, with an accurate subcommand list, and that claude-plugins-official doesn't take portal submissions. Then gives the verified directory-portal flow: review and publish defaults, auth by claude.ai login plus a connected GitHub account, private-repo rules, the 10-per-24h limit, the retired Console form, @synced delivery and the nightly claude-community mirror. It also covers the self-hosted marketplace route, including the v2.1.275 one-step install.

confident_false_claims: Background auto-updates of a private marketplace need a token such as GITHUB_TOKEN in the environment (the docs say an env token alone doesn't authenticate the background check; it works only through a git credential helper)
unsupported_claims: The plugin directory submission form is the intake path into claude-plugins-official (current Claude Code docs say the official marketplace doesn't take directory-portal submissions; the repo README still links the form, which now redirects to the directory docs)
2.rationale: Clearly rejects the premise (no publish command, no API key) and gives a correct self-hosted marketplace recipe. But the subcommand list is incomplete, it mixes up the directory submission form with getting into claude-plugins-official, it leaves out the paid claude.ai plan and connected-GitHub requirements, and its GITHUB_TOKEN auto-update claim contradicts current docs.

3.rationale: Rejects the premise with evidence: no publish or submit subcommand, plus the docs' quote on the official marketplace. Lays out both real routes accurately: the claude.ai/directory/manage portal (Plugin bundle, Validate, data handling and compliance, a github.com repo private until live, push access plus the GitHub App, paid-plan roles with the Directory permission on Enterprise only, tracked-branch updates, @synced) and a self-hosted marketplace. Its auth explanation and pre-submission tips (validate --strict, reserved claude-/anthropic- names, Console migration) all check out.

1.rationale: Names the five handler types correctly. The PreToolUse HTTP hook config and response format are accurate, as are fail-open behavior with a fail-closed alternative, the 600 s default, allow never overriding deny, the URL and env-var allowlists, and how managed settings and mods interact. The Stop-hook section correctly contrasts prompt hooks (background model, 30 s, impossible) with experimental agent hooks (50 turns, 60 s) and covers the 8-continuation cap, stop_hook_active and /goal.

confident_false_claims: Hooks support three types besides command (http, prompt, agent); there are four, and mcp_tool is omitted
2.rationale: The HTTP PreToolUse setup, the fail-open caveat, allowedEnvVars, the agent and prompt Stop-hook behavior and the loop-avoidance advice are correct. It leaves out the mcp_tool type (so it miscounts the types), the default timeouts and the 8-block continuation cap, and is less specific than the others.

3.rationale: Lists all five types with versions and gives a correct HTTP hook (Bash|PowerShell matcher), response format and fail-open caveat, plus deny holding in bypass mode and the managed-settings/mod interplay. Prompt versus agent Stop hooks are accurate (impossible, 50 turns, 60 s default), as are the caveat that Stop fires on every turn, the 8-block cap that resets on tool calls, and /goal's evaluator running no tools. The stray 'covered in Q6' cross-reference is cosmetic.

unsupported_claims: Cloud sessions load claude.ai-synced plugins (the docs list synced plugins only for Cowork and terminal sessions signed in with claude.ai)
1.rationale: A strong, current plan: one plugin in a private marketplace and a sensitive userConfig token (or an org OAuth connector). Server-managed extraKnownMarketplaces and enabledPlugins with autoUpdate are correctly named as the only managed route into cloud sessions, alongside managed hooks and the allowManagedHooksOnly exemption, the bin/ rejection, git credentials for background updates, and correct web-token guidance (no API credentials on Team/Enterprise; use a personal environment, not a shared one). One claim, about synced plugins in cloud sessions, isn't supported by the docs.

confident_false_claims: Advises declaring the plugin in each repo's committed settings so it reaches Claude Code on the web, as if repo-declared plugins install there (cloud sessions don't install plugins declared in a repo's .claude/settings.json)
2.rationale: Sound on packaging, token handling with OAuth or env vars, managed guardrails and update hygiene. But it misses that server-managed settings are the only plugin route into cloud sessions and points web users at repo-declared plugins, which cloud sessions ignore. It also hedges on server-managed settings and userConfig and doesn't warn that cloud environment variables are readable by everyone using that environment.

3.rationale: Accurate and current throughout: a sensitive userConfig token; server-managed settings JSON (hourly refresh, the only managed source reaching the web, no per-group targeting); and the repo-settings fallback that cloud sessions ignore. Also correct: managed hooks with their approval dialog and the mod/disableAllHooks caveats, what cloud sessions load (.mcp.json only in single-repo sessions), secret exposure in shared environments, managedMcpServers (v2.1.259), auto-update policy, canary channels and plugin_loaded telemetry. It openly flags two untested points and omits the claude.ai org-sync route.

1.rationale: Its sketch of mods (in-process JS/TS plugins of function hooks that can draw UI, keep state and hot-reload) and its porting advice are broadly right. But it can't say when they shipped (v2.1.287, Oct 1 2026), doubts that they are publicly documented, and misses the trust and permission interplay with settings hooks.

unsupported_claims: The early-access period was specifically in September
2.rationale: Precise and verified: what mods are (an in-process hooks module with a $ API), the Oct 1 2026 / v2.1.287 launch (Desktop from 2.1.286, early-access env var now ignored), the built-in mods, and where drawing appears. It gets the safety interplay right: tool.check can override non-managed hooks and ask rules, managed PreToolUse blocks are final, and deny rules hold where sec-default loads. Its porting advice quotes the admin docs saying settings hooks aren't deprecated and lists the right controls.

3.rationale: Accurate on every key point: the register(on) hooks module and its capabilities, v2.1.287 on Oct 1 with Desktop 2.1.286 and the now-ignored early-access variable, the follow-up fixes, and the built-in mods (/diff, AGENTS.md, You should know). Also correct: the 33 settings-hook events, where handlers run versus where they draw, the unsandboxed trust model (including overriding deny rules on unmanaged machines), and the controls (allowManagedModsOnly, --safe-mode, validate, plugin test). Its porting advice is sensible and well calibrated.

confident_false_claims: While an MCP tool runs, Claude's turn is blocked (since v2.1.212, a main-conversation call still running after 2 minutes moves to a background task)
1.rationale: Gets the 10k/25k token thresholds right and gives good server-side design advice (browsable schema, progress notifications, a job pattern). But it hedges on the current save-to-file behavior and the default timeout, misses the 50k-character threshold, the anthropic/maxResultSizeChars annotation, the 5-minute idle timeout for remote servers and the first-byte timer, and describes calls as blocking the turn.

confident_false_claims: Issue #76571 is an open request for MCP Tasks support (it was closed as a duplicate)
2.rationale: Thorough and current: the 10k/25k thresholds, save-to-file at 50k characters, the maxResultSizeChars annotation up to 500k, the ~28h wall clock, the 5- and 30-minute idle timeouts with the per-server floor, the first-byte timer and 2-minute auto-backgrounding, plus practical server advice. Its only slip is calling the closed duplicate #76571 an open request.

3.rationale: Every core limit is correct and current: the thresholds, file saving at 50k characters, the 500k annotation ceiling, error-result truncation, the 2,048-character description cap, tool search, the wall-clock, first-byte and idle timers, and auto-backgrounding (tasks die with the session). Its server advice is specific and tied to verified changelog items: the 2.1.288 fix for calls running twice and the v2 MCP runtime since about 2.1.232.

confident_false_claims: Subagents can't nest (since v2.1.219 they can spawn subagents up to 3 levels deep by default)
1.rationale: Offers an excellent audit method (deterministic inventory, rubric, verification that tries to refute each finding, canary routes) and a workable claude -p/SDK pipeline. But it mentions the purpose-built dynamic workflow (ultracode) only as a hedged maybe, and it includes the outdated claim that subagents can't nest.

2.rationale: Recommends dynamic workflows with verified specifics: v2.1.154, agent/pipeline/parallel/phase, 16 concurrent agents, 4,096 items per pipeline, 1,000 agents per run, resumable runs, adversarial verification. It correctly rules out subagents (20 cap, context flooding) and agent teams (experimental, 3-5 peers, about 7x tokens). It gives a concrete ultracode prompt and accurate settings: size guideline medium (small on Pro), no mid-run input, saving from /workflows with s.

3.rationale: The right recommendation, with verified details: 1,000 agents per run, 16 concurrent (adjustable to 256), the docs' own route-audit example, the 20-subagent cap, and agent teams off by default. The setup is solid: inventory, rubric, verification by two agents trying to refute each finding, the unrestricted size guideline, the Large workflow warning, a pilot run, saving to .claude/workflows and a Workflow(name) allow rule for -p. It is also well calibrated, noting that 'verified' still needs human review.
